subject: Chemistry
name: Chemical Thermodynamics

sections.tx: State functions are those which depend only upon the state of the system Temperature, volume, pressure and number of moles are examples
sections.slip: The path taken does not matter for a state function.

sections.tx: Intensive properties are independent of the amount of substance Temperature, pressure, density, concentration, boiling point, freezing point, viscosity
sections.slip: Water always boils at 100 degrees, whether it is 2 litres or 10.

sections.tx: Delta U = Q + W Delta U is internal energy, Q is heat, W is work done
sections.slip: Change in internal energy equals heat added plus work done on the system.

sections.tx: Isothermal: temperature constant Adiabatic: no heat exchange Isobaric and isochoric are the other two
sections.slip: Isothermal keeps T fixed; adiabatic keeps heat fixed at zero exchange.

sections.tx: A wall separates the system from the surroundings There are adiabatic walls and diathermic walls
sections.slip: The wall decides whether heat can cross it.

sections.tx: Enthalpy is denoted delta H It is defined only in chemical reactions at constant pressure Q is defined in any type of process
sections.slip: Delta H is heat change specifically at constant pressure.

sections.tx: Delta H less than 0 means exothermic Delta H greater than 0 means endothermic, energy is absorbed
sections.slip: Negative enthalpy releases heat; positive enthalpy absorbs it.

sections.tx: Extensive properties depend on the amount of substance Volume, mass, total energy, Gibbs free energy, entropy and internal energy
sections.slip: More substance means a bigger value.

sections.tx: Internal energy is the energy contained within any set of molecules It can be bond energy, rotational energy, and more
sections.slip: Internal energy is the total energy already stored inside the molecules.

questions.q: A process has ΔH = 200 J mol^–1 and ΔS = 40 JK^–1 mol^–1. Out of the values given below, choose the minimum temperature above which the process will be spontaneous:
questions.s: To find the minimum temperature for spontaneity, use ΔG = ΔH − TΔS and set ΔG < 0, giving T > ΔH/ΔS. Here, ΔH = 200 J/mol and ΔS = 40 J/K·mol, so T > 200/40 = 5 K. Hence, the process becomes spontaneous at temperatures above 5 K.

questions.q: What is the maximum mass (approximately) which can be raised by 1 meter height by 1 mole of ideal gas if the pressure of gas can be reduced to half of original value and temperature of reservoir is kept constant at 300 K. (g = 10 m/s^2, ln 2 = 0.693)
questions.s:
"THIS IS A HIGH WEIGHTAGE TOPIC"
 For maximum work, the process is to be considered reversible.
\[w = - \int {pdV} = - nRT\ln \frac{{{V_2}}}{{{V_1}}}\]
Since pressure is reduced to half of original value, volume will be doubled. Thus,
\[\left| w \right| = 8.31 \times 300 \times \ln 2 \approx 1727.65{\text{ J}}\]
Now, the work done by the gas is used in raising the given mass.
\[\left| w \right| = mgh\]
\[ \Rightarrow 1727.65 = m \times 10 \times 1\]
\[ \Rightarrow 172.765{\text{ }}kg = m\]

 Standard enthalpy of formation, \[{\Delta _f}{H^ \circ }\] is defined as the amount of energy released/absorbed when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard state.
(a) does not represent \[{\Delta _f}{H^ \circ }\] as the standard state of Carbon is graphite.
(c) does not represent \[{\Delta _f}{H^ \circ }\] as two moles of ammonia are formed.
(d) does not represent \[{\Delta _f}{H^ \circ }\] as carbon dioxide is formed from carbon monoxide which is not an element but a compound.
questions.sub: Enthalpies for Different Types of Reactions

questions.q: The standard enthalpy of formation of NH_3 is –46 kJ mol^-1, If the enthalpy of formation of H_2 from its atoms is -436 kJ mol^-1 and that of N_2 is -712 kJ mol^-1, the average bond enthalpy of N–H bond in NH_3 is
questions.s:
\[\text{Enthalpy of formation of NH}_3 = -46 \,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\]
\[\frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{N_2(g)} + \frac{3}{2}\,\mathrm{H_2(g)} \;\longrightarrow\; \mathrm{NH_3(g)}, \quad \Delta H = -46 \,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\]
\[\mathrm{H_2(g)} \;\longrightarrow\; 2\mathrm{H(g)}, \quad \Delta H = +436 \,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\]
\[\mathrm{N_2(g)} \;\longrightarrow\; 2\mathrm{N(g)}, \quad \Delta H = +712 \,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\]
\[\Delta H = \Sigma \text{B.E. (reactants)} - \Sigma \text{B.E. (products)}\]
\[\Delta H = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\text{B.E. (N}_2) + \tfrac{3}{2}\,\text{B.E. (H}_2) - \text{B.E. (NH}_3)\]

\[-46 = \tfrac{1}{2}\times 712 + \tfrac{3}{2}\times 436 - 3\,( \text{N-H})\]
\[\text{B.E. (N-H)} = +352 \,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\]

The heat of vaporisation of a liquid at 500 K and 1 atm pressure is 10 kcal/mole. What will be the change in internal energy (∆U) in kcal for vaporisation of 3 moles of liquid at the same temperature? [Take R = 2 cal/mol-K, assume gas to be ideal]
questions.s:
"THIS IS A HIGH WEIGHTAGE TOPIC"
 Given - \[\Delta {H_{vap}} = 10\;{\text{kcal/mole}}\]
Thus, enthalpy change for 3 moles of liquid = \[\Delta H = 3 \times 10 = 30{\text{ kcal}}\]
Now, the process can be represented as 3A(l) $\to$ 3A(g)
\[\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta {n_g}RT\]
\[ \Rightarrow 30 = \Delta U + \frac{{3 \times 2 \times 500}}{{1000}}\]
\[ \Rightarrow 30 = \Delta U + 3\]
\[ \Rightarrow \Delta U = 27{\text{ kcal}}\]

questions.q:
Entropy change of $4F{e_{\left( s \right)}} + 3{O_{2\left( g
\right)}} \to 2F{e_2}{O_{3\left( s \right)}}$ is -549.4 J.K^-1.mol^-1 at 298 K. ∆H° for this reaction is -1648 kJ/mol. ∆S_Total will be in kJ.K^-1.mol^-1. (Report the answer to the nearest integer)
questions.s:
"THIS IS A HIGH WEIGHTAGE TOPIC"

For a spontaneous reaction, total entropy must be greater than zero i.e. positive
$4Fe\left( s \right) + 3{O_2}\left( g \right) \to 2F{e_2}{O_3}\left( s \right)$ 
$\Delta {H_f} = - 1648KJ{\text{ mo}}{{\text{l}}^{ - 1}}$ 
Reaction is exothermic and surroundings absorbed 1648 KJ of heat
$\Delta {S_{surr}} = \frac{{\Delta {H_f}}}{T} = \frac{{1648}}{{298}} = 5.53KJ{\text{ mo}}{{\text{l}}^{ - 1}}{k^{ - 1}}$ 
$ = 5530J{\text{ mo}}{{\text{l}}^{ - 1}}{k^{ - 1}}$ 
$\Delta {S_{total}} = \Delta {S_{system}} + \Delta {S_{surrounding}}$ 
$ = - 549.4 + 5530$ 
$ = 4980.6J{k^{ - 1}}mo{l^{ - 1}}$ 
$ = 4.98KJ\,\,{k^{ - 1}}mo{l^{ - 1}}$

questions.q: At 500 kbar pressure, density of diamond and graphite are 3 g/cc and 2 g/cc respectively, at certain temperature ‘T’. Find the value of \[\left| {\Delta H - \Delta U} \right|\] (in kJ/mole) for the conversion of one mole of graphite to 1 mole of diamond at 500 kbar pressure. [Given: 1 bar = 10^5 N/m^2]
questions.s:
Given pressure = 500 kbar = 500 × 10^3 × 10^5 N/m^2 = 5 × 10^10 N/m^2
Now, the mass of one mole of diamond = graphite = 12 g
Thus, volume of one mole of graphite = \[\frac{{mass}}{{density}} = \frac{{12}}{2} = 6{\text{ cc = 6 }} \times {\text{ 1}}{{\text{0}}^{{\text{-6}}}}{\text{ }}{{\text{m}}^{\text{3}}}\]
And volume of one mole of diamond = \[\frac{{mass}}{{density}} = \frac{{12}}{3} = 4{\text{ cc = 4 }} \times {\text{ 1}}{{\text{0}}^{{\text{-6}}}}{\text{ }}{{\text{m}}^{\text{3}}}\]
For conversion of one mole of graphite to diamond,
\[\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta PV\]
\[ \Rightarrow \Delta H - \Delta U = 5 \times {10^{10}} \times \left( {4 - 6} \right) \times {10^{ - 6}} = - 10 \times {10^{10}} \times {10^{ - 6}} = - {10^5}\,{\text{J}}\]
Thus, \[ \Rightarrow \left| {\Delta H - \Delta U} \right| = \,{\text{ }}{10^5}\,{\text{J = 100 kJ}}\]

flashcards.a: Denoted DELTA H Defined ONLY in chemical reactions at CONSTANT PRESSURE Q is defined in any type of process
flashcards.note: Delta H is heat change specifically at constant pressure.

flashcards.a: Delta H LESS THAN 0 means EXOTHERMIC Delta H GREATER THAN 0 means ENDOTHERMIC, energy is absorbed
flashcards.note: Negative enthalpy releases heat; positive enthalpy absorbs it.

flashcards.a: Depend on the AMOUNT of substance Volume, mass, total energy, Gibbs free energy, entropy, internal energy
flashcards.note: More substance always means a bigger value.

flashcards.a: DELTA U = Q + W Delta U is internal energy Q is heat W is work done
flashcards.note: Change in internal energy equals heat added plus work done on the system.

flashcards.a: ISOTHERMAL: temperature is constant ADIABATIC: no heat is exchanged ISOBARIC and ISOCHORIC are the other two
flashcards.note: Isothermal keeps T fixed; adiabatic keeps heat exchange at zero.

flashcards.a: Independent of the AMOUNT of substance Temperature, pressure, density, concentration, boiling point, freezing point, viscosity
flashcards.note: Water always boils at 100 degrees, whether it is 2 litres or 10.

flashcards.a: The energy contained within any set of molecules It can be bond energy, rotational energy, and more
flashcards.note: Internal energy is the total energy already stored inside the molecules.

flashcards.a: Depend ONLY on the STATE of the system Temperature, volume, pressure and number of moles are examples
flashcards.note: The path taken to reach that state does not matter.

flashcards.a: A WALL separates the system from the surroundings ADIABATIC WALL and DIATHERMIC WALL
flashcards.note: The wall decides whether heat can cross between system and surroundings.
